title: “them that believe” (2 Thessalonians 1:10) — Tischendorf’s Greek has a past-tense participle
summary: KJV 2 Thessalonians 1:10 says Christ will be admired “in all them that believe”. The Textus Receptus text served prints the present participle πιστευουσιν; Tischendorf’s text prints the aorist participle πιστεύσασιν, “those who believed”.
text: KJV 2 Thessalonians 1:10: “When he shall come to be glorified in his saints, and to be admired in all them that believe (because our testimony among you was believed) in that day.” Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) 2 Thessalonians 1:10: ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐνδοξασθῆναι ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις αὐτοῦ καὶ θαυμασθῆναι ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς πιστεύσασιν, ὅτι ἐπιστεύθη τὸ μαρτύριον ἡμῶν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς, ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ. Greek New Testament (Textus Receptus as served, printed there without accents) 2 Thessalonians 1:10: ... και θαυμασθηναι εν πασιν τοις πιστευουσιν οτι επιστευθη το μαρτυριον ημων εφ υμας εν τη ημερα εκεινη Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/53/1/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/53/1/.
reasoning: The KJV “them that believe” follows the present participle πιστευουσιν of the TR text. Tischendorf’s πιστεύσασιν is aorist, which a literal English reading gives as “those who believed” or “having believed”, a group defined by an act of belief already completed rather than by continuing belief.
scope: T applies at 2 Thessalonians 1:10 only. The difference is between Greek editions: the Textus Receptus text served agrees with the KJV and Tischendorf’s text does not. This record does not say which reading is original, and two digital editions are not a survey of manuscripts. The Greek New Testament wording is Tischendorf’s eighth edition as served by bolls.life (TISCH), compared with the Textus Receptus text served there (TR); neither is a critical apparatus. Only the word named is compared; other small differences in the verse are not claimed.
